sections.h2: Where is College Park, and what kind of housing market does that create?
sections.html:
College Park is a city in Prince George's County, about 4 miles northeast of Washington, D.C. It covers 5.68 square miles, and the University of Maryland takes up roughly 41% of that area.

That single fact shapes almost every house sale in town. Wikipedia reports a median age of 21.7 and says students make up about 55% of residents, so a large share of the housing stock is built, bought or rented with the campus in mind. A seller here is often dealing with a house that has tenants, a rental history, or a buyer pool of investors rather than families.

The city grew out of land platted in 1872 and replatted in 1889. It was incorporated in 1945, and it has used a council-manager form of government since 1960. The 2020 Census counted 34,740 residents and 11,539 housing units, with 16.8% of those units vacant.

sections.h2: Who employs people in College Park?
sections.html:
The University of Maryland, College Park is the largest employer by a wide margin, with 14,505 employees in 2023, which Wikipedia puts at 49.2% of city employment. Federal agencies fill most of the rest of the list.

  • UMD Global Campus: 1,037 employees
  • NOAA: 900
  • FDA: 755
  • National Archives and Records Administration: 732
  • IKEA: 500
  • IonQ: 200

Part of this activity sits in the Discovery District, a 150-acre business and research park split between College Park and Riverdale Park. It hosts NOAA's Weather Prediction Center and an FDA food safety center, along with quantum computing and cybersecurity firms. A $2 billion public-private effort called Greater College Park started in 2014 and has brought new housing, hotels and a new City Hall (2021).

For a seller, the practical point is that demand follows the academic calendar and federal hiring more than it follows a typical suburban pattern. A house listed in a slow month may sit longer, and a house with a tenant on a lease that ends in May or August has a natural timing constraint.

sections.h2: Which College Park neighborhoods might your house be in?
sections.html:
College Park has more than a dozen named neighborhoods, and the 1945 incorporation boundary alone includes Calvert Hills, Old Town, Lakeland, Berwyn, Branchville, Oak Springs, Daniel's Park and Hollywood, plus Sunnyside.

West of Baltimore Avenue you find Lord Calvert Manor, College Park Woods, Crystal Springs, Acerdale (University View), Autoville, Cherry Hill and Camden. East of the CSX tracks are College Park Estates and Yarrow. Camden and Sunnyside sit outside the Capital Beltway.

Tell any buyer which neighborhood the house is in and whether it has been rented, because that affects the permit questions covered below.

sections.h2: What does College Park's weather and storm history mean for an older house?
sections.html:
College Park has a humid subtropical climate, with a mean daily high of 88.7 degrees F in July and 43.4 degrees F in January. Average annual precipitation is 43.73 inches.

The weather event most local sellers know about is the F3 tornado of September 24, 2001, which Wikipedia says caused 2 deaths, 55 injuries and $101 million in damage. Roofs, siding and trees are the usual repair items on houses of that era. Paint Branch and Indian Creek meet in the southeast corner of the city to form the Northeast Branch Anacostia River, so a buyer or title company may ask whether a property near a stream sits in a mapped flood zone. Check FEMA's map for your address before you assume either way.

If the roof or basement needs work and you do not want to pay for it before selling, an as-is sale to a cash buyer removes the repair negotiation from the process.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit affect a College Park house sale?
sections.html:
College Park is one of the easier Maryland cities to reach without a car, and that is a selling point you can state plainly. The College Park, UMD Metro station serves the Green and Yellow lines, and MARC commuter trains stop beside it. U.S. Route 1 (Baltimore Avenue) runs through the city, MD 193 and MD 431 serve it, and I-95/I-495 is reachable from North College Park.

The Purple Line light rail is under construction between New Carrollton and Bethesda. The project site describes a 16-mile route with 21 stations and reports construction as 92% complete, and Wikipedia lists five stations planned for College Park. A house near a future station may be priced with that in mind, so ask a licensed agent or appraiser how buyers are treating it before you set expectations.

sections.h2: Does College Park require a permit to rent out a house, and what happens when you sell?
sections.html:
Yes. College Park runs its own occupancy permit program, and Prince George's County does not license rentals inside the city. The county's single-family rental page lists College Park among municipalities where the county does not issue rental licenses.

Under the city's code, an owner needs an occupancy permit before renting to anyone outside the immediate family. Key points from the chapter:

  • The permit is issued to the owner for the structure and lasts one year, then renews each year.
  • The city inspects each unit at least once a year, and more often after a substantiated complaint.
  • Living in a unit without a valid permit is prohibited, and unpermitted properties may be placarded.
  • The permit cannot be transferred to another person or entity, and the chapter does not say what happens to it on a sale.

Because the chapter is silent on sales, a buyer of a rented house should expect to apply for their own permit. If you are a landlord selling, confirm with the city whether your permit is current, whether any citations are open, and whether the tenant has to be told about the sale. Overdue fees or an open placard can slow a closing.

sections.h2: What does property tax look like for a College Park owner?
sections.html:
The combined fiscal 2026 rate for a College Park property is $1.6730 per $100 of assessed value, according to the Maryland Department of Legislative Services. That figure appears to add the county rate of $0.9640, a city rate of $0.3350 and a special rate of $0.3740. The county applies a municipal tax rate differential inside incorporated towns, which lowers the county portion there.

Prince George's County says overdue bills accrue interest and penalties of 1.67% each month, and unpaid taxes can lead to a lien and a tax sale. Its homestead credit limits taxable assessment growth on owner-occupied homes to 3% for FY2026, with a 10% state ceiling.

The State Department of Assessments and Taxation reports that Prince George's County properties were reassessed for January 1, 2026, with a 10.3% average increase over January 1, 2023. Increases are phased in evenly over three years, and decreases take effect in full in the first year.

sections.h2: What do you have to tell a buyer in Maryland?
sections.html:
Most sellers of a one-to-four unit home must give the buyer either a property condition disclosure statement or a disclaimer statement, on a form from the State Real Estate Commission. This comes from Maryland Real Property Code section 10-702.

A disclaimer states that the property is sold as is, but it still has to reveal known latent defects that threaten health or safety. If the seller does not deliver the statement before the contract is signed, the buyer may rescind in writing within 5 days of receiving it. The section also lists exemptions, such as transfers by a fiduciary administering an estate, so an inherited College Park house sold by a personal representative is generally treated differently. Ask the estate's attorney which form applies.

sections.h2: What do sellers in College Park usually run into?
sections.html:
Sellers here tend to meet the same short list of problems, and a few of them come straight from the student-rental economy.

  • Tenants on a lease, and a buyer who wants vacant possession.
  • Wear from years of shared occupancy that a retail buyer will ask you to repair.
  • An occupancy permit that lapsed, or a city inspection with open items.
  • Inherited houses where the family lives elsewhere and no one has kept up the yard or roof.
  • Back taxes or a lien that has to be paid from the proceeds at settlement.

A cash sale does not erase any of these, but it can change who has to fix them. A cash buyer that purchases as is takes on the repair list, and you can ask whether the buyer will accept tenants in place. Get the closing date, who pays the county transfer tax and what is being left behind in writing before you sign.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental permit from College Park to sell a rented house?
faqs.a: You do not need a permit to sell, but a rented house should have a valid city occupancy permit while it is rented. The code says the permit is not transferable, so the buyer applies for a new one if they will keep renting.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a house sale in College Park?
faqs.a: Prince George's County lists a 1.4% transfer tax in the legislative services rate table. Who pays it, and how it is split with the state portion, is set in the contract, so confirm it with the title company.

faqs.q: How much is the property tax rate in College Park?
faqs.a: The fiscal 2026 combined rate is $1.6730 per $100 of assessed value in the Department of Legislative Services table. Your own bill depends on your assessed value and on any homestead credit.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in College Park with tenants still living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. The house can be sold with tenants in place, and the lease usually passes to the new owner. If the buyer wants it empty, you will need to follow Maryland landlord-tenant rules and the lease terms.

faqs.q: Is College Park in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of the area sit near Paint Branch and Indian Creek, so some properties may be mapped. Look up your specific address on FEMA's flood map, because the city as a whole is not one zone.
